title: CallPlay: ergonomic cross-language function invocation helpers and resilient streaming
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a developer-facing helper library (CallPlay) across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to make function-schema validation, invocation, retries, and streaming ergonomics consistent and safer. Focus on: (1) pairing model-declared function schemas with runtime validators, (2) creating an idempotent invocation token and dedupe layer for at-least-once streaming, (3) backpressure-aware client helpers for resumable streaming responses, and (4) small language-specific ergonomic wrappers (async generators in Python, async iterables in TS, channel-based primitives in Go).
acceptance_criteria: Library exposes consistent API for registering function schemas and invoking functions across Python/TS/Go
Automatic schema validation runs before the first request and converts typed inputs to schema-compatible payloads
Streaming helper can resume from last acked message using idempotency token and checkpoint metadata
Retries obey per-call policy with exponential backoff + jitter and are transparent to caller unless fatal error
Documentation includes language-specific examples and a guided migration path from existing invoke helpers
tasks: Draft design doc and example idioms (Python async generator, TS async iterable, Go channel)
Implement schema normalizer (server-compatible shapes + type hints) in each SDK
Build idempotency token manager and resume-point checkpointing in runtime helper
Add retry policy layer (P0 defaults + per-call override) and surface telemetry hooks
Write end-to-end integration tests with streaming simulator and flaky network scenarios
Author docs, code samples, and migration guide; create dev-rel examples repo
notes: Motivation: many teams misuse function schemas or mix typed structs with free-form args causing runtime failures; we want early validation and helpful errors
Tradeoffs: strict validation avoids runtime model errors but can prevent graceful degradation for unknown future schema fields; propose an opt-in permissive mode
Design decision: default to 'validate-and-coerce' rather than 'strict-fail' for first release to reduce customer breakage
Telemetry: emit validation_result + retry_count + resume_attempts to sdk-telemetry topic
Compatibility: ensure wire schema remains unchanged (helpers operate client-side) so Hosted/Dedicated customers need no server upgrade
implementation_snapshot: TS: CallPlay.registerSchema(schema) -> CallPlay.call(name, args, {idempotencyToken, retryPolicy}) returns AsyncIterable for streaming responses
Go: callplay.Register(schema) returns a typed Invoker with Call(ctx, args, options) -> (<-chan StreamEvent, error)
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema coercion and validation with edge-case types (nulls, large ints, nested arrays)
Simulated flaky stream runner to validate resume semantics and checkpoint durability
Chaos tests toggling transient 5xxs and network drops with telemetry asserts
Integration smoke in hosted sandbox + Dedicated internal cluster before rollforward
rollout_plan: Feature gate default: off for customers on older SDKs; opt-in via CallPlay.enable(true) in SDK config
Internal dogfood: enable for Redwood Console integrations and a subset of internal ML infra routes for 2 weeks
Gradual rollout: 10% -> 33% -> 100% across Hosted endpoints with flagged experiments for retries/resume metrics
feedback: PM review (Amir Patel): prefer conservative retry defaults; require explicit enable for resume by default
Design review (Rhea Singh): suggested adding 'safety_level' param to map model-facing options to runtime coercion levels
Security review (N/A): no direct secrets handling; ensure idempotency tokens are ephemeral and not logged
open_questions: How should helper surface schema evolution warnings vs errors? (soft-warning channel vs exception)
Should we ship SDK-side 'per-field sanitizer' presets for common types (email/uuid/timestamp)?
What's the expected retention window for resume checkpoints in Dedicated vs Hosted?
